title: The Hands That Kept It
summary: Keep a workshop company alive as the Recall reaches Tessell. Rescue fitters, defend repair yards and earn the salvage that turns four patched walkers into a force with a say in who owns them.

opening.title: Four names on a list
body: The Recall arrives during the night shift at Sarn's Gantry Three. Its four serials are the walkers standing in your yard. Records keeper Iona Venn has barred Marker Eleven's registry door against Kestrel's compliance team. She is still copying the margins: fitters' names, repaired joints, generations of work that the seizure list calls someone else's property.

You command Linewrought. The guns are mismatched and the workshops know every patch. Venn has kept one crated Aurelian optic out of the inventory; Halloran will release it if your company opens the registry. Bring people and useful equipment home. Your first foothold is a place with a door, a name and someone waiting behind it.

chapters.title: The lamp from Marker Eleven
body: Venn comes out carrying a copy of the rolls and a crated Focused Medium Laser. The workshop marks its receipt 'Marker Eleven'. That source remains in the company report even after the emitter becomes a working gun. This is Halloran's released stock; whatever you recover from the cordon is a separate claim.

The next main job leads to fitter Nera Pell at Cut Nine. In the bay, the new one-box emitter can replace a Gadfly's left-arm Flamer without changing weight. Save it as Lamplighter if that job suits the machine. It can cover the recovery winch from farther back; its hotter shot still needs discipline. The optional reader survey remains available before the rescue.

chapters.title: A crew brought home
body: Pell's crew rides the cradle out of Cut Nine. They sign over a damaged, unarmed Prybar hulk and ask for a lift home to Gantry Three. The company has gained a machine it can rebuild and equip, not a free combat-ready walker. Pell recognises the emitter from Venn's cabinet: her workshop replaced its cooling jacket two winters ago.

Kestrel is following. The next lift allows 205 tonnes, exactly your original four. A lighter rebuilt machine can change the detail, but someone must pilot it and something must guard the gantry while a runner fetches stores. Decide what the company can field before accepting that division of labour.

chapters.title: Gantry Three finishes its shift
body: Pell restarts the gantry's traverse as the last carrier stops. Venn pins the copied rolls beside the shift board. One registry cabinet, one recovery lift and one working repair hall now belong to the same service trail. Your company carried a piece of that trail into battle in whatever form you chose to keep it.

Sarn honours its workshop access and the next main posting opens. Keeping Gantry Three working has bought the company more than a fee: people who know its machines, a place willing to repair them and evidence that these roots were never abandoned by everyone.

chapters.title: White armour in the yard
body: The first Aurelian claim detail is beaten. Its precise emitters and factory-fitted armour are real advantages; so are the gaps your company found in its formation. Halloran has waived its share of the recoverable Stock. If a machine survives recovery, it can fight beside yours. The common mounts accept mixed weapons; heat, ammunition and scarce replacements still have to be paid for.

chapters.title: A rule worth keeping
body: Sarn retains the recording of Kestrel firing after an ejected pilot. The Ironmuster Code gives the ground-holder the wreck. It also gives the pilot a way home. Breaking that second rule threatens every crew on Tessell, including yours. Kestrel has lost the yard, but its cut to Sarn's power trunk has left the western repair halls cold.

chapters.title: Power and proof
body: The load transfers and the repair halls regain power. Among Sarn's service records is an address leading toward the old depot manifest: the clearest surviving record of Tessell's walker roots. Halloran wants the approach opened. Your company is now strong enough to reach evidence that could decide the Recall, rather than merely survive its next contract.

chapters.title: Behind the depot doors
body: Barrow is open. The master manifest can be held intact, giving Tessell evidence and making the company its keeper. It can be burned, denying the Authority its strongest seizure record while destroying a century of service history with it. Halloran got the company through the door. It cannot choose what the company is willing to carry.
These are alternative endings. Either concludes the campaign without requiring every optional posting.

chapters.title: A claim without a ledger
body: The master manifest burns. The Recall loses its strongest seizure record, and Tessell’s workshops gain time to decide their own future. The same fire takes certified service histories, witness chains and proof that could have supported local stewardship.

Sarn’s gantries remain lit, but every future claim will be argued from scattered copies and living memory. The company leaves Barrow as the force that made the choice. Its victory is real and its responsibility permanent.

chapters.title: Keepers of the record
body: The manifest survives under the company’s seal. Tessell has evidence that its workshops maintained the roots the Continuance abandoned, and the Authority must negotiate with people it first counted as inventory. The record does not erase copied serials or the shortages beyond Tessell. It prevents either side from erasing the other.

Sarn’s gantries remain lit. The rescued fitters return machines to service, including captured Stock when the parts can be made to fit. The company leaves Barrow stronger and answerable for what the record is used to justify.
